job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

passage: In a recent study on human physiology, researchers highlighted how our internal systems function continuously to maintain life. Contrary to popular belief, the human heart does not purify blood; it acts solely as a mechanical pump to circulate blood throughout the body, while the lungs facilitate gas exchange. Meanwhile, the digestive system is highly specialized. The small intestine is lined with finger-like projections called villi, which significantly increase the surface area for nutrient absorption rather than just providing a smooth surface for food transit. Furthermore, cellular respiration is a constant process occurring in all living cells, not just in the lungs. Even during intense exercise, human muscle cells perform anaerobic respiration to generate energy when oxygen supply is limited, proving this process is not exclusive to yeast or bacteria. Finally, the kidneys function as complex filtration units. They do not simply act as a passive sieve; they selectively reabsorb essential substances like glucose and water back into the blood, ensuring that only metabolic waste products are excreted as urine. This distinguishes true excretion from the simple elimination of undigested food waste, which is a separate digestive process. These findings clarify that our organs perform specific, highly regulated biological roles to sustain our survival every single second.

items.evidence: Contrary to popular belief, the human heart does not purify blood; it acts solely as a mechanical pump to circulate blood throughout the body, while the lungs facilitate gas exchange.
items.q: Meena says the heart cleans blood. What is the heart's real job?
options: It pushes blood around the whole body
It makes fresh blood for the body
It takes in oxygen from the air
It filters waste out of the blood
items.explain: The heart is only a pump that moves blood around; it does not purify or make blood.

wrong.why: thinks the heart creates or purifies blood
mixes up the heart with the lungs
gives the heart the kidney's filtering job

items.evidence: The small intestine is lined with finger-like projections called villi, which significantly increase the surface area for nutrient absorption rather than just providing a smooth surface for food transit.
items.q: Why does the inner wall of the small intestine have finger-like villi?
options: To give a larger area for absorbing food
To make a smooth path for food to slide
To break food into pieces by rubbing it
To store food until the body needs it
items.explain: Villi increase the surface area so more nutrients can be absorbed, not to make a smooth surface.

wrong.why: thinks the intestine is smooth so food slides
thinks villi grind food like teeth
thinks the intestine only stores food

items.evidence: Even during intense exercise, human muscle cells perform anaerobic respiration to generate energy when oxygen supply is limited, proving this process is not exclusive to yeast or bacteria.
items.q: A sprinter's muscles are running low on oxygen. What do the muscle cells do?
options: They still release energy without oxygen
They stop releasing energy until oxygen returns
They pass the work to the lungs to make energy
They cannot respire, since only yeast can
items.explain: Muscle cells perform anaerobic respiration to make energy when oxygen is limited, just like yeast or bacteria.

wrong.why: thinks cells need oxygen to make any energy
thinks energy is made in the lungs
thinks anaerobic respiration is only in yeast

items.evidence: They do not simply act as a passive sieve; they selectively reabsorb essential substances like glucose and water back into the blood, ensuring that only metabolic waste products are excreted as urine.
items.q: How do the kidneys keep useful glucose from leaving the body in urine?
options: They take it back into the blood
They let it fall through like a sieve
They push out all the liquid they filter
They turn it into waste before removal
items.explain: Kidneys selectively reabsorb glucose and water into the blood, so only waste leaves as urine.

wrong.why: thinks the kidney is a simple sieve
thinks all filtered liquid is removed

items.evidence: This distinguishes true excretion from the simple elimination of undigested food waste, which is a separate digestive process.
items.q: Which example shows true excretion, as the passage describes it?
options: Kidneys removing metabolic waste in urine
The gut passing out undigested food
The lungs making energy while we breathe
The kidney passing out all liquid it filters
items.explain: Excretion removes metabolic waste, such as urine from the kidneys; passing undigested food is a separate digestive process.

wrong.why: thinks excretion means getting rid of undigested food
thinks energy is made in the lungs
thinks the kidney removes all filtered liquid
